questions.question: What is push-based architecture?

options.text: Server proactively sends data to clients when events occur, without clients asking

questions.explanation: Push: server initiates communication. When event happens, server pushes to interested clients. Examples: WebSockets, push notifications, pub/sub. Real-time, but requires maintaining connections/subscriptions.

questions.question: What is pull-based architecture?

options.text: Clients request data when they need it; server responds to requests

questions.explanation: Pull: client initiates. Client asks 'give me updates', server responds. Examples: HTTP requests, polling, REST APIs. Simple, stateless, but may miss events or waste resources polling.

questions.question: When would you choose push over pull?

options.text: When real-time updates are critical and data changes frequently

questions.explanation: Push for: real-time needs (chat, live scores, trading), frequent updates, many interested clients. Avoids polling overhead. Tradeoff: connection management, handling disconnections, scaling subscribers.

questions.question: When would you choose pull over push?

options.text: When data changes infrequently, clients need data on-demand, or simplicity is valued

questions.explanation: Pull for: infrequent updates, on-demand data needs, simple architecture, stateless servers. Examples: checking email, loading web pages, API calls. Simpler to implement and scale.

questions.question: What is the main disadvantage of polling (pull)?

options.text: Wasted resources when no updates; delayed detection of changes between polls

questions.explanation: Polling problems: most polls return 'no change' (wasted requests), updates detected only at next poll interval (latency). High frequency = more waste. Low frequency = more delay. Lose-lose.

questions.question: What is the main disadvantage of push?

options.text: Complexity of maintaining connections, handling disconnections, and scaling to many subscribers

questions.explanation: Push challenges: maintain persistent connections (memory, file descriptors), handle disconnections gracefully, scale to millions of subscribers, ensure delivery. More complex infrastructure.

questions.question: What is long polling?

options.text: A hybrid where client polls but server holds request open until data is available or timeout

questions.explanation: Long polling: client requests, server waits (holds connection) until update available, then responds. Client immediately re-requests. Simulates push over HTTP. Used before WebSockets were common.

questions.question: How does Prometheus collect metrics?

options.text: Prometheus pulls (scrapes) metrics from application endpoints

questions.explanation: Prometheus: pull-based. Scrapes /metrics endpoints at configured intervals. Advantages: simpler apps (just expose endpoint), Prometheus controls rate, works through firewalls. Push gateway for short-lived jobs.

questions.question: How do push notifications work on mobile?

options.text: Device maintains connection to platform service (APNs/FCM); server pushes to platform, platform pushes to device

questions.explanation: Mobile push: device maintains one connection to Apple/Google. Your server sends to APNs/FCM, they push to device. Efficient: one connection for all apps, platform handles delivery. True push.

questions.question: What is the 'thundering herd' problem with pull?

options.text: Many clients polling simultaneously, overwhelming the server with requests

questions.explanation: Thundering herd: if all clients poll at same interval starting same time, requests bunch up. Solutions: jitter (randomize poll times), exponential backoff, or switch to push for high-scale scenarios.

questions.question: What is fan-out in push systems?

options.text: Distributing a single update to many subscribers

questions.explanation: Fan-out: one event → many recipients. Celebrity tweets to millions of followers. Challenge: delivering quickly to all. Solutions: async processing, message queues, hierarchical distribution.

questions.question: A social media feed needs to show new posts. Push or pull?

options.text: Hybrid: push for active users, pull on app open; or pull with smart caching

questions.explanation: Social feeds often hybrid: push new posts to timeline cache (fan-out on write), pull when user opens app (fan-out on read for celebrities). Balance real-time feel with scalability. Twitter/Facebook use hybrid.
